ankle.context: A foot in side view with the ankle joint marked. Used in physiotherapy and sports injury apps, orthopedic clinic pages, symptom checkers and body-part pickers.

baby-feet.context: Two small footprints side by side, the size of a baby's. Common on birth announcements, baby registries, maternity and newborn care pages and parenting apps.

back-body.context: A torso seen from behind, with the spine and shoulder blades drawn in. Used for back pain in symptom checkers, physiotherapy and posture apps, massage menus and body maps.

beard.context: A full beard joined to a moustache, drawn without the rest of the face. Barbershops, grooming and shaving products, avatar builders and style guides use it.

belly-button.context: A torso with the navel marked at its centre. Found in anatomy references, body maps in symptom checkers, piercing studio menus and pregnancy or fitness apps.

bicep.context: An arm bent at the elbow with the biceps flexed. Used for strength training, gym and workout apps, fitness goals and anything meaning strong or tough.

bladder.context: The urinary bladder drawn as an anatomical organ. Used in urology and continence care, urinary health content, medical diagrams and symptom checkers.

blood-drop.context: A single drop of blood. Used for blood donation drives, blood type and blood test results, bleeding or injury warnings and period or cycle trackers.

bone.context: A single bone. Shows up in orthopedic and fracture content, bone health and calcium information, anatomy apps and dog treat or pet shop menus.

brain.context: A brain seen from the side, with its folds drawn in. Used for thinking, ideas and intelligence, neurology and psychology content, memory training and AI or machine learning tools.

cell.context: A living cell with its nucleus in the middle. Biology lessons, life sciences and lab software, microbiology and stem cell research content all use it.

chest.context: A bare torso showing the chest muscles. Used for chest workouts in fitness apps, body maps and symptom checkers, and upper-body sizing in clothing guides.

dna.context: Two twisting strands joined by rungs, the DNA double helix. Common in genetics and ancestry tests, biology and biotech content, research labs and topics about identity or origin.

elbow.context: An arm bent at the elbow with the joint marked. Used for elbow pain and injury in physiotherapy apps, sports medicine, orthopedic pages and body maps.

eye-closed.context: A closed eye with lashes along the lid. Used to hide a password or private content, for sleep and rest modes, blink detection and eye health apps.

eyebrow.context: An eye with a raised eyebrow above it. Brow shaping and beauty salons, makeup tutorials and reactions that show doubt or curiosity use it.

eyelashes.context: An open eye fringed with long eyelashes. Used by beauty salons and lash studios, mascara and makeup products, cosmetics shops and eye-care apps.

foot.context: A human foot in side view. Used for podiatry and foot care, walking or step counts, shoe size guides and body maps.

head.context: A human head in side profile. Used for people and profile sections, mind and thinking topics, headaches in symptom checkers and silhouette avatars.

knee.context: A bent leg with the knee marked. Used for knee pain, sports injuries, knee replacement and physiotherapy, and body maps.

leg.context: A leg and foot in side view. Lower-body workouts, leg injuries and body maps, walking and mobility, and inseam or length guides for clothing all use it.
